content.comment_body: I have a running [product_name] here, with a program that displays some timer settings on the device screen. I am unable to connect using [product_name] software. How can I view or modify the IP address of the [product_name] while it is still operational? Currently, I can view inputs, outputs, and flags via the display using the cursor, but can't locate where to stop the program or adjust the network configuration.

Welcome to the forum. If the [product_name] is in RUN mode, you cannot change its IP address or subnet mask. This is only possible when the device is in STOP mode, and you must be in administrator mode for these changes.

Is a UTP connection required to stop the [product_name]? That seems to be my issue—the IP address stored in the software does not connect to the device. Is there no way to display the current IP from the device in running mode or to stop the device remotely? Do I need to replace it to resolve this?

You do not require a UTP connection; a standard ethernet cable will work. What is your goal? Do you wish to go online and change the IP address using the software, or do you want to adjust it directly on the device?

I am using the standard ethernet cable for [product_name], assuming it's UTP, but still cannot connect to the running device. It appears to have an unfamiliar IP address and subnet mask, and has been operating for a year. I tested with another [product_name], which connects without issues, so the cable, adapter, and administrator mode are not the problem. The address book in the software is set to 192.168.0.3 with subnet 255.255.255.0 and gateway 192.168.0.0. How can I update the program on this older running device without knowing its IP address? Is there a way to read it or stop the device and change its IP without using ethernet? The display only shows programmed text related to timers, set by a previous colleague. While running, only inputs, outputs, and flags are accessible via the cursor. How do I set the IP address on this device?

You can set the IP address and subnet mask directly on the device, but only in administrator mode. In operator mode, you may view the IP address but cannot modify it; changes require STOP state and administrator access. To switch the device to STOP, you must enter administrator mode, usually by knowing the password (default password is often "LOGO"). If you are viewing input/output status, pressing the ESC key will take you to the main menu. In administrator mode, the menu will show "Stop" at the top; in operator mode, "Program" is at the top instead. If you see "Program," select "Setup" and then "Switch to ADMIN," enter the password, and press OK. If accepted, you'll be in administrator mode and able to proceed.
That worked, thank you. Holding ESC a bit longer in the input/output view allowed access, unlike before.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced problems connecting to a [product_name] device with configuration software, due to not knowing its current IP address and being unable to alter network settings while the device was running. They sought a way to manage these settings without halting operation or relying on network connection. Advice focused on switching to administrator mode to stop the device, which enables changes to network parameters. The step-by-step instructions helped resolve the user’s confusion, and another device confirmed the issue was not hardware-related.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to view or modify the IP address of their [product_name] device while it is running, or at least find a way to retrieve or change the address without requiring network access or stopping the device unexpectedly.
